title: The Carpenter's Corner
story:
James woke to the soft, rhythmic patter of rain drumming against the mossy red tiles of the old timber shed. He sat up in the cool, cedar-scented quiet, letting his gaze trace the familiar beams overhead where dust motes danced in the pale morning light filtering through the doorway. It was a space that belonged to no one and yet welcomed him entirely, offering a dry sanctuary far from the bustling towers of Oakhaven.

Stepping out from the threshold as the morning drizzle settled into a light mist, James found this man at work beneath the open-air eaves of the main workshop. The elder was carefully planing a length of rough-hewn pine, sending thin, pale curls of wood tumbling gracefully toward the packed dirt floor. James watched the steady, practiced motion of the hands, noting the quiet patience written into every stroke of the blade.

Without a word, this man paused his work, offering a gentle nod of recognition and sliding a small wooden stool closer to the workbench. James climbed up to sit, resting his paws on the cool, sanded surface as he reached into his canister to retrieve his charcoal and map. Together, in the quiet heart of Aldea San Gabriel, they spent the morning shaping the raw edges of wood and charcoal alike, turning the slow hours into a shared language of craft.
location: The Old Shed behind Don Tadeo's Workshop, Aldea San Gabriel
